title: When Writing Style Drifts: Benchmarking Authorship Verification under Distribution Shifts in Genre, Time and the AI-Era
abstract: arXiv:2608.17979v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Authorship verification (AV) assumes that an author's writing style remains sufficiently stable to distinguish it from that of other writers. In practice, however, this assumption is challenged by distribution shifts caused by changes in genre, time, and AI-assisted writing. Existing AV benchmarks typically study these factors in isolation and focus predominantly on English, limiting our understanding of model robustness under realistic conditions. We introduce AVShift, the first German benchmark for systematically evaluating AV under multiple distribution shifts. AVShift comprises over 150,000 text pairs spanning three genres and 21 years, enabling controlled evaluation of cross-genre, temporal, and AI-era shifts within a unified framework. translated_title: 当写作风格发生漂移：体裁、时间与AI时代分布偏移下的作者身份验证基准测试
translated_abstract: 作者身份验证（AV）假设作者的写作风格足够稳定，以便将其与其他作者区分开来。然而，在实践中，这一假设受到由体裁变化、时间变化和AI辅助写作引起的分布偏移的挑战。现有的AV基准测试通常孤立地研究这些因素，且主要聚焦于英语，限制了我们对模型在现实条件下鲁棒性的理解。我们引入了AVShift，这是首个用于系统评估多种分布偏移下AV的德语基准测试。AVShift包含超过15万个文本对，跨越三种体裁和21年时间，能够在统一框架内对跨体裁、时间性和AI时代偏移进行受控评估。我们对代表性的基于特征、基于嵌入和基于大语言模型的方法进行了基准测试。实验表明，微调的大语言模型在跨体裁泛化方面表现最佳，并显著受益于风格特征。
tldr: 本文提出了首个德语作者身份验证基准AVShift，统一评估跨体裁、时间和AI时代分布偏移，发现微调大语言模型在跨体裁泛化上表现最优且受益于风格特征。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces AVShift, the first German benchmark for authorship verification under multiple distribution shifts, and finds that fine-tuned LLMs generalize best across genres and benefit from stylistic features.
